sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This procedure ensures the organisation responds to a breach of unsecured protected health information correctly and within the timelines the HIPAA Breach Notification Rule requires.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: All suspected or confirmed breaches of unsecured PHI.

sections.heading: 3. Assess Whether a Breach Occurred
sections.body:
An impermissible acquisition, access, use or disclosure of unsecured PHI is presumed a breach unless a documented risk assessment shows a low probability that PHI was compromised. The four-factor assessment considers:
- The nature and extent of the PHI involved, including the types of identifiers.
- The unauthorised person who used the PHI or to whom it was disclosed.
- Whether the PHI was actually acquired or viewed.
- The extent to which the risk to the PHI has been mitigated.

sections.heading: 4. Notify Individuals
sections.body: Affected individuals are notified without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery, with the information the rule requires.

sections.heading: 5. Notify HHS
sections.body: The Secretary of Health and Human Services is notified: within 60 days for breaches affecting 500 or more individuals, and annually for smaller breaches.

sections.heading: 6. Notify the Media
sections.body: For a breach affecting more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction, prominent media outlets are notified without unreasonable delay and within 60 days.

sections.heading: 7. Business Associates
sections.body: A business associate notifies the covered entity of a breach without unreasonable delay and within 60 days. [FILL IN: name who coordinates breach response.]

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This business associate agreement sets out the terms HIPAA requires when a business associate creates, receives, maintains or transmits protected health information on behalf of a covered entity (or another business associate).

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: The relationship between the covered entity and the business associate, and the PHI the business associate handles.

sections.heading: 3. When a BAA Is Required
sections.body:
A business associate agreement is put in place before a business associate creates, receives, maintains or transmits protected health information (PHI) on the covered entity's behalf. Sharing PHI without a signed agreement in place is not permitted.
[FILL IN: identify the business associates you use and the PHI each one handles.]

sections.heading: 4. Required Terms
sections.body: The agreement includes the terms required by 45 CFR 164.504(e). At a minimum, the business associate:

rows: The business associate uses or discloses PHI only as permitted by the agreement or required by law
It implements appropriate safeguards, including the Security Rule requirements for ePHI
It reports security incidents and breaches of unsecured PHI to the covered entity
It ensures subcontractors that handle PHI agree to the same restrictions and conditions
It assists with access, amendment and accounting of disclosures
It makes its practices, books and records available to HHS
On termination, it returns or destroys all PHI where feasible
The covered entity may terminate if the business associate breaches a material term

sections.heading: 5. Parties and Scope
sections.body:
The agreement identifies the parties, the services the business associate provides, and the PHI involved, so the scope of permitted use is clear.
[FILL IN: name the parties and the services covered.]

sections.heading: 6. Term and Termination
sections.body: The agreement states its effective date and term, and the covered entity may terminate it if the business associate breaches a material term and does not cure it. On termination, the business associate returns or destroys all PHI where feasible, and where it is not feasible, extends the protections of this agreement to the retained PHI and limits further use.

rows: Puts BAAs in place and tracks them.

sections.heading: 8. Compliance & Enforcement
sections.body: Compliance with this policy is mandatory. Violations may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or contract, and may be reported to relevant authorities where required by law.

sections.heading: 9. Exceptions
sections.body: Any exception to this policy must be requested in writing, risk-assessed, and approved by [Approver / CISO] at [Company Name]. Approved exceptions are documented, time-bound and reviewed at expiry.

sections.heading: 10. Review
sections.body: This policy is reviewed at least annually, or after a significant change or security incident, and updated as required.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This contingency plan ensures the organisation can respond to an emergency or other occurrence that damages systems containing electronic protected health information, as the HIPAA Security Rule requires (164.308(a)(7)).

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: The systems and ePHI that support critical operations.

sections.heading: 3. Data Backup Plan
sections.body:
Retrievable, exact copies of ePHI can be recovered after a loss:
- Backups of ePHI are created on a defined schedule and protected (including against ransomware).
- Backups are stored so a single event cannot destroy both the data and its backup.
- Restoration from backup is tested so it is known to work.
- [FILL IN: your backup scope, frequency and restore-test cadence.]

sections.heading: 4. Disaster Recovery Plan
sections.body: Procedures restore any loss of ePHI and the systems that hold it, within defined recovery time and recovery point objectives, prioritising the most critical applications and data.

sections.heading: 5. Emergency Mode Operation Plan
sections.body: Procedures enable critical business processes to continue, and the security of ePHI to be protected, while the organisation operates in emergency mode (for example during an extended outage).

sections.heading: 6. Testing and Criticality Analysis
sections.body: The plan is tested and revised periodically, and the criticality of applications and data is assessed to prioritise recovery.

sections.heading: 7. Activation and Roles
sections.body: The plan defines who can declare an emergency, the team responsible for executing it, and how they are contacted, so the response can be invoked quickly when systems holding ePHI are affected. [FILL IN: your activation authority and contacts.]

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy implements the HIPAA minimum-necessary standard, so uses, disclosures and requests of protected health information are limited to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: All uses, disclosures of and requests for PHI, except where the standard does not apply.

sections.heading: 3. Role-Based Access
sections.body:
Access to PHI is limited so that workforce members see only what their job requires:
- For each role, the categories of PHI it needs and the conditions of access are defined.
- Access is granted against those role definitions and removed when a role changes or ends.
- [FILL IN: define the role-based access to PHI in your organisation.]

sections.heading: 4. Routine Disclosures and Requests
sections.body:
Recurring uses, disclosures and requests are constrained by design:
- Routine and recurring disclosures and requests are limited to the minimum necessary through standard protocols.
- Non-routine or one-off disclosures and requests are reviewed individually against the minimum-necessary standard.
- When requesting PHI from others, the organisation likewise asks only for the minimum necessary.

sections.heading: 5. Exceptions
sections.body:
The minimum-necessary standard does not apply to:
- Disclosures to, or requests by, a health-care provider for treatment.
- Disclosures to the individual who is the subject of the PHI.
- Uses or disclosures made under a valid authorisation, to HHS, or as required by law.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy governs how the organisation uses and discloses protected health information (PHI) and how it respects individuals' rights, as the HIPAA Privacy Rule requires.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: All PHI the organisation maintains, in any form, and all workforce members who handle it.

sections.heading: 3. Uses and Disclosures
sections.body:
PHI is used and disclosed only where the Privacy Rule permits:
- For treatment, payment and health-care operations.
- As otherwise permitted or required by law (with the conditions the rule sets).
- Otherwise, only with the individual's valid written authorisation.

sections.heading: 4. Minimum Necessary
sections.body: Uses, disclosures and requests are limited to the minimum necessary to accomplish the purpose, except where the minimum-necessary standard does not apply (such as treatment, or disclosures to the individual).

sections.heading: 5. Notice of Privacy Practices
sections.body: A Notice of Privacy Practices describing how PHI is used and individuals' rights is provided and posted. [FILL IN: reference your Notice of Privacy Practices.]

sections.heading: 6. Individual Rights
sections.body:
Individuals can exercise their rights:
- Access and obtain a copy of their records within the required timeframe.
- Request amendment of their records.
- Request an accounting of disclosures and restrictions on uses and disclosures.
- Complain without retaliation.

sections.heading: 7. Safeguards and Training
sections.body: Reasonable safeguards protect PHI, workforce members are trained, and complaints are handled.

rows: Ensure their teams understand and follow the policy.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy establishes the sanctions applied to workforce members who fail to comply with the organisation's HIPAA policies and procedures, as the Security Rule requires.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: All workforce members who handle PHI or ePHI.

sections.heading: 3. Sanctions
sections.body:
Failures to comply with the organisation's HIPAA policies and procedures result in disciplinary action:
- Action is proportionate to the nature and severity of the violation, up to and including termination.
- Sanctions are applied consistently and documented.
- [FILL IN: reference your disciplinary scale or tiers.]

sections.heading: 4. Process and Records
sections.body: Suspected violations are investigated, the appropriate sanction is decided and applied, and the record of the violation and the action taken is retained for six years. Sanctions are not applied to a workforce member for filing a good-faith complaint, assisting an investigation, or opposing an unlawful practice, nor for exercising HIPAA rights.

sections.heading: 5. Consistency and Awareness
sections.body: Sanctions are applied consistently regardless of a workforce member's seniority, in proportion to the nature and severity of the violation, and the workforce is made aware that failing to comply with HIPAA policies carries consequences.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy implements the administrative, physical and technical safeguards the HIPAA Security Rule requires to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of electronic protected health information (ePHI).

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: All ePHI the organisation creates, receives, maintains or transmits, and the systems and workforce that handle it.

sections.heading: 3. Administrative Safeguards
sections.body:
The organisation maintains administrative safeguards:
- A security management process, including a risk analysis and risk management.
- An assigned security official responsible for the policy.
- Workforce security and information access management on least privilege.
- Security awareness and training, security incident procedures and a contingency plan.
- A periodic evaluation of safeguards.

sections.heading: 4. Physical Safeguards
sections.body:
Physical safeguards protect facilities, workstations and devices:
- Facility access controls and workstation use and security.
- Device and media controls covering disposal, re-use, accountability and backup.

sections.heading: 5. Technical Safeguards
sections.body:
Technical safeguards protect ePHI in systems:
- Access control with unique user IDs, automatic logoff and encryption where appropriate.
- Audit controls, integrity controls and authentication.
- Transmission security, including encryption of ePHI in transit.
- [FILL IN: name your EHR and key systems and their controls.]

sections.heading: 6. Business Associates and Documentation
sections.body: Business associates are bound by agreements, and policies and records are retained for six years.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy ensures all workforce members receive security and privacy awareness training, as the HIPAA Security and Privacy Rules require.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: All workforce members, including employees, volunteers and trainees, who handle PHI.

sections.heading: 3. Training Programme
sections.body:
Training is provided and documented:
- To each new workforce member within a reasonable time of joining.
- Periodically thereafter, and when policies or systems change materially.
- Covering security awareness (malware, log-in monitoring, passwords) and privacy obligations.
- [FILL IN: state your training cadence and platform.]

sections.heading: 4. Security Reminders and Role-Specific Content
sections.body:
Training is reinforced and made relevant:
- Periodic security reminders are issued to the workforce between formal training sessions.
- Content is tailored to a member's role and level of access to PHI, so it reflects the risks they actually handle.
- Topics include guarding against, detecting and reporting malicious software, monitoring log-in attempts, and managing passwords.

sections.heading: 5. Records
sections.body: Training assignment and completion are documented and retained for six years, and non-completion is followed up so coverage can be demonstrated.
